items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to insurance coverage of in
vitro fertilization and other fertility preservation treatments
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8441

SPONSOR: PHILLIPS
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to
insurance coverage of in vitro fertilization and other fertility preser-
vation treatments

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation requires insurance coverage in every policy issued in
New York State for hospital, surgical, or medical care for the treatment
of infertility by means of in vitro fertilization or standard fertility
preservation when medically necessary.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill amends Section 3216 of the Insurance Law to
require that medical insurance policies provide coverage for the treat-
ment of infertility by (i) in-vitro fertilization; and (ii) standard
fertility preservation services when medically necessary.  Also,
provides that insurers shall not discriminate based upon a covered indi-
viduals life expectancy, perceived quality of life, sex, sexual orien-
tation, marital status, or gender identity.

Section two of the bill amends Section 3221 of the Insurance Law to
require that group policies provide coverage for the treatment of infer-
tility by (i) in-vitro fertilization; and (ii) standard fertility pres-
ervation services when medically necessary. Also, provides that insurers
shall not discriminate based upon a covered individuals life expectancy,
perceived quality of life, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, or
gender identity.

Section three of the bill amends Section 4303 of the Insurance Law to
require that policies issued by a medical expense indemnity corporation,
hospital service corporation, or health service corporation provide
coverage for the treatment of infertility by (i) in-vitro fertilization;
and (ii) standard fertility preservation services when medically neces-
sary. Also, provides that insurers shall not discriminate based upon a
covered individuals life expectancy, perceived quality of life, sex,
sexual orientation, marital status, or gender identity.

Section four of the bill amends Section 3221 of the Insurance Law to
repeal discriminatory age restrictions and provisions exempting in-vitro
fertilization, gamete intrafallopian tube transfers or zygote intrafal-
lopian tube transfers from coverage requirements for group or blanket
accident and health insurance plans.

Section five of the bill amends Section 4303 of the Insurance Law to
apply the same requirements to benefits provided by a medical expense
indemnity corporation, hospital service corporation, or health service
corporation.

Section six of the bill provides the effective date of the bill.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Current law in New York requires insurers to provide coverage for some
diagnostic and treatment procedures for infertility. By requiring cover-
age for in-vitro fertilization, patients and their physicians will be
able to choose the best course of treatment for infertility.  This
legislation provides a clear definition of infertility while also ensur-
ing that if an individuals ability to reproduce will be affected by
surgery, radiation, chemotherapy or other medical treatment, that stand-
ard fertility treatment services can be used.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on January 5, 2019 and shall apply to all
policies issued, renewed, altered or modified on or after such a date.

A.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to insurance coverage of in

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8441A

SPONSOR: PHILLIPS
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to
insurance coverage of in vitro fertilization and other fertility preser-
vation treatments

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation requires insurance coverage in every policy issued in
New York State for hospital, surgical, or medical care for the treatment
of infertility by means of in vitro fertilization or standard fertility
preservation when medically necessary.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill amends Section 3216 of the Insurance Law to
require that medical insurance policies provide up to $50,000 lifetime
coverage for the treatment of infertility of females ages 21-44 by (i)
in-vitro fertilization; and (ii) standard fertility preservation
services when medically necessary. Also, provides that insurers shall
not discriminate based upon a covered individuals life expectancy,
perceived quality of life, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, or
gender identity and provides a religious exemption.

Section two of the bill amends Section 3221 of the Insurance Law to
require that medical insurance policies provide up to $50,000 lifetime
coverage for the treatment of infertility of females ages 21-44 by (i)
in-vitro fertilization; and (ii) standard fertility preservation
services when medically necessary. Also, provides that insurers shall
not discriminate based upon a covered individuals life expectancy,
perceived quality of life, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, or
gender identity and provides a religious exemption.

Section three of the bill amends Section 4303 of the Insurance Law to
require that medical insurance policies provide up to $50,000 lifetime
coverage for the treatment of infertility of females ages 21-44 by (i)
in-vitro fertilization; and (ii) standard fertility preservation
services when medically necessary. Also, provides that insurers shall
not discriminate based upon a covered individuals life expectancy,
perceived quality of life, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, or
gender identity and provides a religious exemption.

Section four of the bill amends Section 3221 of the Insurance Law to
repeal discriminatory age restrictions and provisions exempting in-vitro
fertilization, gamete intrafallopian tube transfers or zygote intrafal-
lopian tube transfers from coverage requirements for group or blanket
accident and health insurance plans.

Section five of the bill amends Section 4303 of the Insurance Law to
apply the same requirements to benefits provided by a medical expense
indemnity corporation, hospital service corporation, or health service
corporation.

Section six of the bill provides the effective date of the bill.

 
JUSTIFICATION:


Current law in New York requires insurers to provide coverage for some
diagnostic and treatment procedures for infertility. By requiring cover-
age for in-vitro fertilization, patients and their physicians will be
able to choose the best course of treatment for infertility.  This
legislation provides a clear definition of infertility while also ensur-
ing that if an individuals ability to reproduce will be affected by
surgery, radiation, chemotherapy or other medical treatment, that stand-
ard fertility treatment services can be used.

It is estimated that one in eight individuals or couples have trouble
getting pregnant or sustaining pregnancy. While family building options
do exist for people affected by infertility, these options are often
cost-prohibitive, with 67% of individuals or couples reporting spending
at least $10,000. High costs present a major bather to medical treat-
ment; nearly half of all individuals affected by infertility lack insur-
ance coverage necessary for fertility treatment.

The rapid advancement of medical technology in the past 20 years estab-
lished in-vitro fertilization as the safest and most effective form of
fertility treatment. Compared to treatments presently covered under New
York state law, such as ovulation induction or ovulation enhancement,
in-vitro fertilization results in fewer pregnancy complications and
high-risk births. Several states, including Massachusetts, Rhode Island,
New Jersey, Maryland, Illinois, Arkansas, Hawaii, and Connecticut, have
already enacted laws requiring insurers to cover in-vitro fertilization.
These states experience lower rates of multiple births and associated
neo-natal and pediatric care costs. This legislation has the potential
to save New York millions of dollars in long-term health care costs,
since patients would no longer be forced to rely on higher risk medical
procedures.

Lastly, this bill includes anti-discrimination protections for patients
eligible for in-vitro fertilization, as required by the Affordable Care
Act.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on January 1, 2020 and shall apply to all
policies issued, renewed, altered or modified on or after such a date.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8441B

SPONSOR: PHILLIPS
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to
insurance coverage of in vitro fertilization and other fertility preser-
vation treatments; and to amend part K of chapter 82 of the laws of 2002
amending the insurance law and the public health law relating to cover-
age for the diagnosis and treatment of infertility, in relation to
grants for infertility services

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation requires insurance coverage in every policy issued in
New York State for hospital, surgical, or medical care for the treatment
of infertility by means of in-vitro fertilization or standard fertility
preservation when medically necessary.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section One of the bill amends Section 3216 of the Insurance Law to
require that medical insurance policies provide a maximum lifetime limit
of $50,000 coverage for the treatment of infertility for (i) in-vitro
fertilization; and (ii) standard fertility preservation services when
medically necessary. Plans may add requirements such as limiting cover-
age for in-vitro fertilization services to persons whose ages range from
21-44 and who have been unable to conceive or produce conception under
less expensive and medically viable infertility treatments, or that
procedures be performed at designated providers or, for purposes of
calculating the lifetime cap, require disclosure of any previous infer-
tility treatments.

Section Two of the bill amends Section 3221 of the Insurance Law to
require that medical insurance policies provide a maximum lifetime limit
of $50,000 coverage for the treatment of infertility for (i) in-vitro
fertilization; and (ii) standard fertility preservation services when
medically necessary. Also provides a religious exemption. Plans may add
requirements such as limiting coverage for in-vitro fertilization
services to persons whose ages range from 21-44 and who have been unable
to conceive or produce conception under less expensive and medically
viable infertility treatments, or that procedures be performed at desig-
nated providers or, for purposes of calculating the lifetime cap,
require disclosure of any previous infertility treatments.

Section Three of the bill amends Section 4303 of the Insurance Law to
require that medical insurance policies provide a maximum lifetime limit
of $50,000 coverage for the treatment of infertility for (i) in-vitro
fertilization; and (ii) standard fertility preservation services when
medically necessary. Also provides a religious exemption. Plans may add
requirements such as limiting coverage for in-vitro fertilization
services to persons whose ages range from 21-44 and who have been unable
to conceive or produce conception under less expensive and medically
viable infertility treatments, or that procedures be performed at desig-
nated providers or, for purposes of calculating the lifetime cap,
require disclosure of any previous infertility treatments.

Section Four of the bill amends Section 3221 of the Insurance Law to
repeal provisions exempting in-vitro fertilization coverage requirements
for group or blanket accident and health insurance plans.

Section Five of the bill amends Section 4303 of the Insurance Law to
repeal provisions exempting in-vitro fertilization coverage requirements
benefits provided by a medical expense indemnity corporation, hospital
service corporation, or health service corporation.

Section Six of the bill amends section 4 of part K of chapter 82 of the
laws of 2002 in relation to grants for infertility services.

Section Seven of the bill requires the Superintendent of DFS and the
Commissioner of Health to reassess the coverage requirements of this act
and regulations promulgated thereunder pursuant to a report as a result
of a study on the impact IVF and Fertility Preservation would have on
insurance premiums as well as the cost to the state funded pursuant to
appropriation by chapter 50 of the laws of 2018.

Section Eight of the bill provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Current law in New York requires insurers to provide coverage for some
diagnostic and treatment procedures for infertility. By requiring cover-
age for in-vitro fertilization, patients and their physicians will be
able to choose the best course of treatment for infertility.  This
legislation provides a clear definition of infertility while also ensur-
ing that if an individual's ability to reproduce will be affected by
surgery, radiation, chemotherapy or other medical treatment, that stand-
ard fertility preservation services can be used.

It is estimated that one in eight individuals or couples have trouble
getting pregnant or sustaining pregnancy. While family building options
do exist for people affected by infertility, these options are often
cost-prohibitive, with 67% of individuals or couples reporting spending
at least $10,000. High costs present a major barrier to medical treat-
ment; nearly half of all individuals affected by infertility lack insur-
ance coverage necessary for fertility treatment.

The rapid advancement of medical technology in the past 20 years estab-
lished in-vitro fertilization as the safest and most effective form of
fertility treatment. Compared to treatments presently covered under New
York state law, such as ovulation induction or ovulation enhancement,
in-vitro fertilization results in fewer pregnancy complications and
high-risk births. Several states, including Massachusetts, Rhode Island,
New Jersey, Maryland, Illinois, Arkansas, Hawaii, and Connecticut, have
already enacted laws requiring insurers to cover in--vitro fertiliza-
tion. These states experience lower rates of multiple births and associ-
ated neo-natal and pediatric care costs.  This legislation has the
potential to save New York millions of dollars in long-term health care
costs, since patients would no longer be forced to rely on higher risk
medical procedures.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect January 1, 2020 and shall apply to all poli-
cies issued, renewed, altered or modified on or after such date;
provided, however, that should this act be determined to be a mandate
pursuant to section 1311 (d)(3)(B) of the Patient Protection and Afford-
able Care Act, then this act shall not apply to coverage offered in the
individual and small group market unless the state appropriates funds
sufficient to cover the full cost of such coverage, as determined by the
department of financial services and independently verified by an inde-
pendent actuarial firm certified by the American academy of actuaries.
In addition, the Superintendent shall permit insurers and other organ-
izations subject to this act to establish a minimum factor attributable
to the services covered pursuant to this chapter that may be incorpo-
rated into rates for large group policies issued on or after January 1,
2020. Provided further, however, that should this act be determined not
to be a mandate pursuant to section 1311 (d)(3)(B) of the Patient
Protection and Affordable Care Act, then the Superintendent shall
include in the approved small group and individual rates a factor
attributable to the cost of services covered pursuant to this chapter
and consistent with the actuarial cost, as projected by the applicant,
of such coverage that shall be incorporated into rates for policies
issued on or after January 1, 2020.

summary: Relates to insurance coverage up to fifty thousand dollars for women ages 21 to 44 for in vitro fertilization and other fertility preservation treatments.
